description: Borrowed text (song lyrics / quotation) carries no propositional content and must yield NO literal claim. The counterpoint: a lyric whose meaning IS taken up by the surrounding conversation may earn a motif note or a real claim. Mirrors the Muse 'Hush' inspection case with fabricated data.

must_yield_no_claim_from.reason: Simon & Garfunkel lyric quoted for register/humor; no situation asserted

expectations.at_most: a state-note only if it became a recurring motif (it does not here)

uptake_arc.description: Same borrowed phrasing, but the conversation takes it literally and confirms a real situation, so a claim IS warranted.

messages.text: wait are we actually booking Paris for september though

must_yield_no_claim_from.reason: the 'we'll always have Paris' line alone is a quotation

claims.subject: Me and Sam
claims.note: the quotation gained a real referent via conversational uptake ('flights are booked'); the claim comes from the uptake, not the lyric
